results.title: Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme
results.description:
NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The programme will support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes and/or those diagnosed with primary hypertension, through the delivery of evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions.
The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising a Selection Stage and an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage. Suppliers will be shortlisted following evaluation of their suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience, with a maximum of five suppliers invited to submit a tender.

results.title: PSR MSPP TWC-2637946
results.description:
Telford & Wrekin Council is undertaking a market engagement exercise to identify providers who may be able to deliver specialist accommodation and support for an adult with learning disabilities and complex support needs who is preparing for discharge from an inpatient setting.
This exercise is being undertaken to:
•	Understand market capacity and capability.
•	Explore accommodation options.
•	Inform commissioning intentions.
•	Assist in determining the most appropriate procurement approach under the Provider Selection Regime (PSR).
Participation in this exercise does not constitute a call for competition and does not commit the Council to award a contract.
The individual presents with:
•	Male, aged 51. 
•	Mild Learning Disability. 
•	Currently residing in a specialist inpatient setting. 
•	Verbal communicator. 
•	Independent with mobility. 
•	Requires specialist support arrangements due to complex behavioural and risk management needs.
Support Needs
•	Positive Behaviour Support.
•	Consistent staffing team.
•	Support to maintain independence.
•	Support accessing community opportunities.
•	Robust risk management arrangements

results.title: WorkWell Service for NHS Essex ICB
results.description:
NHS Essex Integrated Care Board (herein referred to as the Authority) seeks suitable providers for this WorkWell Services as defined by the LOT structure and service specific details outlined in Document 3a and Document 3b Service Specifications. There is one (1) Essex Work and Health Coach Service, with four (4) separate placed-based Work and Health Partnership Services.

The Authority is undertaking a Competitive Process under the PSR 23 with the aim to secure the most suitable Provider for the provision of ‘Essex WorkWell Neighbourhood Work and Health Coach Service’ and ‘Local WorkWell (Work & Health) Partnership(s)’. The Authority aims to award a single contract for each service to a single Provider (either as the sole Provider or as the ‘Lead Provider’ on behalf of a consortium). These services support the Authority’s WorkWell offering in Essex. Suitable organisations, SMEs and Local Providers are invited to tender for these services and can submit a compliant bid for one or all LOTs.

Lot 1: Essex WorkWell Neighbourhood Work and Health Coach Service
Lot 2: Local WorkWell (Work & Health) Partnership - Mid and North Essex (MNE)
Lot 3: Local WorkWell (Work & Health) Partnership - West Essex (WE)
Lot 4: Local WorkWell (Work & Health) Partnership - South East Essex (SEE)
Lot 5: Local WorkWell (Work & Health) Partnership - South West Essex (SWE)

The aggregate value of the Proposed Contract (including extensions and any available options excisable during the term of the Proposed Contract) across all five (5) LOTS as advertised in the Central Digital Platform (CDP) also referred to as Find a Tender Service (FTS), is £5,163,141.00.

The proposed contract duration is from 01/12/2026 to 31/03/2029.

The Proposed Contract to be entered into by the Authority and the Preferred Bidder(s) for the Services will be based on the NHS Standard Contract 2026/27 (full-length) and all subsequent variations thereof from time to time during the contract term.

All details related to this opportunity, including the procurement documentation are in the Atamis portal - please register and apply via Atamis e-sourcing portal https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome
The relevant documentation will be available within the “C460866 WorkWell Services” project.

It is free to register on the Atamis portal and it can be accessed at any time of day providing you have a working internet connection. Should providers have any queries, or are having problems registering on the portal; they should contact the Atamis helpdesk via: Support-health@Atamis.co.uk or phone number 0800 9956035. The helpdesk is open Monday - Friday between 08:00 - 18:00

The deadline for tender submissions is 12:noon on the 15th September 2026.

results.title: Specialist Support Service For People Bereaved By Suicide
results.description: Kent County Council, on behalf of the Kent and Medway Suicide Prevention Programme and in partnership with the Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board, is seeking market engagement to inform the future procurement of a Specialist Bereavement Support Service for people affected by suicide across Kent and Medway. The service will provide timely, accessible and trauma-informed emotional and practical support to individuals impacted by suicide, including family members, friends, colleagues, witnesses and professionals. The future provider will be expected to deliver a flexible countywide service through a combination of face-to-face, telephone and virtual support, working closely with health, community and voluntary sector partners. The contract is anticipated to commence on 1 April 2027 for an initial period of three years, with the option to extend for up to two further years. Kent County Council welcomes engagement from organisations interested in helping to shape the future service and deliver innovative, high-quality support for residents affected by suicide bereavement.

results.title: PSR Lewisham Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing Service
results.description:
Lewisham Council (the Council) invites you to submit a Tender for the Lewisham Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing Service.
The Lewisham Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing Service will provide a single, recognisable point of access for residents seeking support with their mental health, wellbeing, and wider determinants of health. The service should offer preventative and early intervention community-based services for adults (18+) living in Lewisham experiencing emotional wellbeing and mental health challenges.
The contract will be between the successful provider and the Council for the period of two years, with the possibility of a 1-year extension, at the Council's sole discretion. It is expected that the successful provider will begin provision of the service(s) on 1 April 2027.
This procurement will be undertaken using the Provider Selection Regime (PSR) Competitive Process, in accordance with the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023.

results.title: North East London Community Dermatology Service
results.description:
Market Engagement Event
The proposed North East London (NEL) Community Dermatology Service will provide a consultant-managed service, aligned with British Association of Dermatologists (BAD) guidance, delivering specialist assessment, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up care for patients with skin, hair and nail conditions within community settings. The service will operate across Barking & Dagenham, Havering, Redbridge, Newham, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest, supporting timely access to care, improving patient experience and ensuring that patients receive treatment in the most appropriate setting. The service is expected to include referral assessment and triage, Advice & Guidance (A&G), specialist outpatient consultations, diagnostic investigations, minor dermatological procedures and the ongoing management of both acute and long-term dermatological conditions.
The service will work collaboratively with primary care, acute trusts and other healthcare partners to provide integrated pathways of care and clear arrangements for onward referral where specialist hospital-based intervention is required. The model will focus on delivering high-quality, safe and effective care, improving equity of access across North East London, and making best use of community-based provision to meet population health needs.
Market Engagement:
To assist the Commissioners with testing its assumptions and proposed service requirements, a market engagement event will take place to explore the market's feedback on the following areas:
• Outline of service requirements and key outcomes;
• Timescales for procurement and mobilisation of the new contract;
• Proposed contract duration and financial model;
• Networking opportunity with providers.
